rows.body: Country Inn & Suites by Radisson is a U.S.-anchored, breakfast-led upper-midscale flag in the Radisson family under Choice—suburban corridors, airport markets, and highway nodes rather than resort or urban lifestyle plays. Dealality census shows a thin CALA footprint today (Costa Rica); owner underwriting should weight domestic supply, Item 19 enterprise mix (~81.8% in FY 2025 sample), and refreshed prototype economics.

rows.title: Americas
rows.body:
Established U.S. scale anchor

North America carries nearly all open Country Inn inventory—suburban, airport, and university-adjacent upper-midscale boxes with complimentary hot breakfast and residential-style lobbies. Choice development press cites six Country Inn openings in 2024, a refreshed prototype, and sharpened brand identity in 2025; owner conversations center on franchise economics versus Comfort and Quality, not core Radisson full-service.

rows.title: CALA
rows.body:
Selective CALA node

Dealality census records one open Country Inn in Costa Rica (San José–Heredia airport corridor)—upper-midscale Radisson-family distribution in Central America, not a broad CALA resort or multi-country expansion story. Confirm authorization geography and local comps before using other Radisson-family CALA openings as analogues.

rows.title: Europe
rows.body:
Heritage context only

Country Inn is franchised in the Americas by Choice; European Radisson-family hotels operate under different ownership structures. Useful for traveler brand recognition—not a template for European greenfield or conversion underwriting on this flag.

rows.title: MEA
rows.body:
Limited direct relevance

No material Country Inn open inventory in MEA on Dealality census paths—treat as international brand-awareness context only, not a regional growth thesis for this flag.

rows.title: APAC
rows.body:
Limited direct relevance

Thin-to-no Country Inn presence in APAC on census-backed paths; domestic U.S. ramp curves and census-backed counts should drive feasibility—not APAC Radisson network density.

U.S. development pipeline momentum

Country Inn growth under Choice is distribution- and prototype-led: the brand compounds when owners want warm, residential upper-midscale with Radisson recognition, high enterprise booking mix, and a value-engineered new-build or conversion box—not upscale full-service or soft-collection flexibility. Public 2024–2025 press (six openings, RevPAR Index gains, 38 pipeline additions) is directional—model your corridor locally.

Country Inn reads as “warm upper-midscale with U.S. scale and thin international nodes”: credible for suburban and airport owner stories where breakfast-led limited-service and Choice Privileges distribution matter more than design-led lifestyle or resort amenity depth. It tends to show best where guests expect residential comfort and operators can defend enterprise and loyalty mix—not where the deal needs meetings-heavy full-service or CALA beach conversion narrative.
